nodes.title: Requests continue to fail after Network Service restarts
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 40.1.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 Enterprise 25H2 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version not sure, but it didnt work on 36.x or 39.x either ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior If Network Service process restarts after a crash, fetch requests made in main/utility process should recover ### Actual Behavior After Network Service crashes and restarts, fetch requests made in main/utility processes continue to fail with `net:ERR_FAILED` ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/ImVeryLost/2d0817dc31ffaa1d89e0c0ccd97b5fe2 ### Additional Information Some of our electron app users report seeing unexplained network service crashes, which log `[60300:0129/140619.088:ERROR:content\browser\network_service_instance_impl.cc:610] Network service crashed or was terminated, restarting service.` (I see there are a few other similar "network service crashed" errors, but this one is on windows. Let me know if i should file a separate one) Service process does restart, but various http requests keep failing. To reproduce, i did the following: 1. Run the Electron fiddle in the attached gist 2. Use Microsoft's [Process Explorer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/process-explorer) to find the electron.exe process, and its subprocess with the utility-sub-type NetworkService 3. Kill this process to simulate a crash 4. Continue watching the Process Explorer - you will see that a new NetworkService sub process appears after a second or two 5. Check the fiddle logs - fetch requests continue to fail long after the service process comes back to life

nodes.title: macOS: Cannot double-click to select package directories (e.g., .ufo) in open dialog with filters
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Tahoe: Version 26.2 (25C56)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

There should be a way to allow package directories (like `.ufo`, `.bundle`, etc.) to be:
- Visible and selectable when matching a filter extension
- Selected via double-click (same as regular files)

### Actual Behavior

I'm building a font editor where I need to load [ufo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_Font_Object) files (which are directories).

When using `dialog.showOpenDialog()` with filters that include a package directory extension (e.g., `.ufo`), there's no way to allow users to both:
1. See the package directory as selectable (not greyed out)
2. Double-click to select it (rather than navigating into it)

## Attempts and results

### 1. With filters only

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory"],
  filters: [{ name: "Fonts", extensions: ["ufo"] }],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` directories are greyed out and cannot be selected.

### 2. With `treatPackageAsDirectory`

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory", "treatPackageAsDirectory"],
  filters: [{ name: "Fonts", extensions: ["ufo"] }],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` directories are selectable via single-click + Open button, but double-clicking navigates into the directory instead of selecting it.

### 3. Without filters

```js
dialog.showOpenDialog({
  properties: ["openFile", "openDirectory"],
});
```

**Result:** `.ufo` can be selected, but so can any other file type, which is not an ideal experience for a user.


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

nodes.title: Linux: app.getGPUInfo throws Error: GPU access not allowed. Reason: GPU access is disabled in chrome://settings
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

22,24

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.3.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron app starts and shows new `BrowserWindow`.

### Actual Behavior

After upgrade from v39.3.0 to v40.0.0 calling `app.getGPUInfo('basic')` throws:
```
Error: GPU access not allowed. Reason: GPU access is disabled in chrome://settings.
```

The code is called before `BrowserWindow` is created (by Sentry.js initialization). We have tried in on 3 different machines (with different graphic cards) with Ubuntu 22 and Ubuntu 24, too.

We use:
```js
app.disableHardwareAcceleration();
```

And without this, the app starts OK. Also when I've tried to add the switch:
```js
app.disableHardwareAcceleration();
app.commandLine.appendSwitch("use-angle", "swiftshader");
```

Then the app starts OK, too. 

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

* Switching from Wayland to X11 by `export XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11` does not help.
* Same problem with v40.0.beta1.
* v40.0.alpha.8 shows the window, but it's blank and console is flooded by "Network service crashed or was terminated, restarting service."
  * => Seems like the problem is in some commit between v40.0.alpha.8 and v40.0.beta1.
* Same problem with electron@v41.0.0-alpha.2

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

22,24

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.3.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron app starts and shows new `BrowserWindow`.

### Actual Behavior

After upgrade from 39.2.3 to 40.0.0 **build** of our Electron app freezes with:
```
This error originated either by throwing inside of an async function without a catch block, or by rejecting a promise which was not handled with .catch(). The promise rejected with the reason:
Error: GPU access not allowed. Reason: GPU access is disabled in chrome://settings.
    at Object.processEvent (/home/.../build/electronapp/linux-unpacked/resources/app.asar/electron/main.js:2:1205174)
    at E.Object.assign.id (/home/.../build/electronapp/linux-unpacked/resources/app.asar/electron/main.js:2:2361453)
    at g.getEventDefaults (/home/.../build/electronapp/linux-unpacked/resources/app.asar/electron/main.js:2:1533195)
    at runNextTicks (node:internal/process/task_queues:64:5)
    at process.processImmediate (node:internal/timers:472:9)
    at async Immediate.<anonymous> (/home/.../build/electronapp/linux-unpacked/resources/app.asar/electron/main.js:2:460843)
ERROR [root] Unhandled process promise rejection Error: GPU access not allowed. Reason: GPU access is disabled in chrome://settings.
<<The previous stacktrace repeated>>
[16455:0126/200518.412410:WARNING:ui/ozone/platform/wayland/common/drm_render_node_path_finder.cc:111] Preferred drm_render_node not found, picking vmwgfx
```

The code freezes in `on `app.whenReady().then(...)` so no `BrowserWindow` is created yet. This does not happen when developing an app with `npx electron .`, but it happens when the code is built with `npx electron-builder --dir` and then the build is run. (Or when *.deb is built and installed.) We have tried in on 3 different machines (with different graphic cards) with Ubuntu 22 and Ubuntu 24, too.

We use:
```js
app.disableHardwareAcceleration();
```

And without this, the app starts OK. Also when I've tried to add the switch:
```js
app.disableHardwareAcceleration();
app.commandLine.appendSwitch("use-angle", "swiftshader");
```

Then the app starts OK, too. 

Switching from Wayland to X11 by `export XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11` does not help.

I am sorry, I've tried to separate the issue into a simple Fiddle project, but could not simulate the issue. We have a bit complicated setup.) Can you help me to do more diagnostic or point where could be a problem so I would be able to isolate it?

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Although I have not a testcase, posting the bug here for the others who hit the same problem.

nodes.title: windows alt+space should get routed through 'system-context-menu' event
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

as per #19429 - there currently is no way to prevent alt+space in windows from opening the system context menu 

even using webContents.on("before-input-event")... though, even if it did, its less than ideal as preventing a keyDown event means that the keyUp will never fire, as per #37336

### Proposed Solution

#19429 proposes allowing an override specifically for alt+space, but I think it might be more meaningful to have the alt+space get routed through the existing "before-input-event" event, as it is more semantically appropriate and (hopefully) should allow the actual relevant keyboard events through.

### Alternatives Considered

I feel the only viable alternative would be as #19429 suggests: have a specific option to override the alt+space keyboard combination, but I think that's less than ideal for the aforementioned reasons.

I have tried using a global hotkey and an accelerator key, but neither were able to allow the key event through to the browser window.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: utilityProcess `exit` event reports incorrect code on Windows
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (10.0.26100 Build 26100)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The `exit` event in `utilityProcess` should include the correct exit code for the process, regardless of how it exits.

### Actual Behavior

If you clone the attached gist and run `npm install && npm run build && npm run start`, you get the following output:
```
Utility process exited with code: 18446744072635812000
```

This also happens if you use the `exit()` function from `cstdlib`, but not if you call `process.exit(0xC0000AA0)` in `utility.js` for some reason.

The correct decimal value would be `3221228192`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/rf-/bbe5ecede1f2b10ac2bed4c46ac66509

### Additional Information

I started looking into this because of a user report about a utility process crash. The logs reported the exit code `18446744072635812000`, which seemed weirdly high and isn't documented anywhere.

I think the issue here is that [exit codes on Windows are 32-bit unsigned integers, a.k.a. `DWORD`s](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-getexitcodeprocess), but [they get passed from Chromium to Electron as `int`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/patches/chromium/feat_enable_passing_exit_code_on_service_process_crash.patch) and then eventually get turned into 64-bit values by first extending the "signed" integer to 64 bits and then reinterpreting it as an unsigned value.

This works fine if the code is low enough to be interpreted as a positive `int`, but if it's interpreted as a negative `int` it gets mangled by the extension to 64 bits. Here's some Rust demonstrating this process:
```
let a: u32 = 0xC0E90002;
println!("{a:x} {a}"); // c0e90002 3236495362

let b: i32 = a as i32;
println!("{b:x} {b}"); // c0e90002 -1058471934

let c: i64 = b as i64;
println!("{c:x} {c}"); // ffffffffc0e90002 -1058471934

let d: u64 = c as u64;
println!("{d:x} {d}"); // ffffffffc0e90002 18446744072651079682
```

Then of course it gets turned into a 64-bit float by JavaScript, which loses precision since the value is so high. This is unfortunate since there are [70 different `NTSTATUS` codes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-erref/596a1078-e883-4972-9bbc-49e60bebca55) that yield my original error code when sent through this process.

I haven't looked too closely at the relevant code on the Electron side, but I think the fix would just be to immediately cast the `int` value we get from Chromium to a `uint` so that subsequent conversions don't misinterpret the value?

### Electron Version

40.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (10.0.26100 Build 26100)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

The `exit` event in `utilityProcess` should include the correct exit code for the process, regardless of how it exits.

### Actual Behavior

If you clone the attached gist and run `npm install && npm run build && npm run start`, you get the following output:
```
Utility process exited with code: 18446744072635812000
```

This also happens if you use the `exit()` function from `cstdlib`, but not if you call `process.exit(0xC0000AA0)` in `utility.js` for some reason.

The correct decimal value would be `3221228192`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/rf-/bbe5ecede1f2b10ac2bed4c46ac66509

### Additional Information

I started looking into this because of a user report about a utility process crash. The logs reported the exit code `18446744072635812000`, which seemed weirdly high and isn't documented anywhere.

I think the issue here is that [exit codes on Windows are 32-bit unsigned integers, a.k.a. `DWORD`s](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-getexitcodeprocess), but [they get passed from Chromium to Electron as `int`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/patches/chromium/feat_enable_passing_exit_code_on_service_process_crash.patch) and then eventually get turned into 64-bit values by first extending the "signed" integer to 64 bits and then reinterpreting it as an unsigned value.

This works fine if the code is low enough to be interpreted as a positive `int`, but if it's interpreted as a negative `int` it gets mangled by the extension to 64 bits. Here's some Rust demonstrating this process:
```
let a: u32 = 0xC0E90002;
println!("{a:x} {a}"); // c0e90002 3236495362

let b: i32 = a as i32;
println!("{b:x} {b}"); // c0e90002 -1058471934

let c: i64 = b as i64;
println!("{c:x} {c}"); // ffffffffc0e90002 -1058471934

let d: u64 = c as u64;
println!("{d:x} {d}"); // ffffffffc0e90002 18446744072651079682
```

Then of course it gets turned into a 64-bit float by JavaScript, which loses precision since the value is so high. This is unfortunate since there are [70 different `NTSTATUS` codes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-erref/596a1078-e883-4972-9bbc-49e60bebca55) that yield my original error code when sent through this process.

I haven't looked too closesly at the relevant code on the Electron side, but I think the fix would just be to immediately cast the `int` value we get from Chromium to a `uint` so that subsequent conversions don't misinterpret the value?

### Electron Version

Windows

### Operating System Version

window10

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Dear Electron team,
I hope this message finds you well. I've encountered a consistent issue where the desktopCapturer.getSources() method is unable to detect a window that is created with the parent parameter specified in its BrowserWindow constructor options.
When the parent parameter is omitted, desktopCapturer.getSources() correctly lists the window in the returned sources array. However, once the parent parameter is set (pointing to a valid parent window), the child window disappears entirely from the sources list returned by desktopCapturer.getSources(), making it impossible to capture the child window's content via screen capture APIs.
This behavior is unexpected and blocks use cases where we need to capture content from child windows that have a parent window association (e.g., modal windows, child panels in desktop apps).

### Actual Behavior

The child window (created with the parent parameter) should be included in the array returned by desktopCapturer.getSources(), just like windows without a parent parameter.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_
